content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: overtime on both queues, callbacks, chat deflection and internal moves lift service level to 81.5% for 13:45-17:15 at ₹14,607 extra cost.","why":"The problem is demand, not staffing. The 12:30 credit card limit upgrade SMS (MKT-2026-951) has pushed general queue calls up 72%, and new_offer_enquiry is running at 5.2x normal. Service level has fallen to 0% with 28 abandons. R2 is the only option that follows policy and reaches the 80% target over the disruption window. It predicts 81.5% overall (general 78.6%, payments 84.9%) and cuts the abandon rate to 4.0%, against 11.5% if we do nothing. Overtime on payments, callbacks, delayed breaks and cancelled payments coaching keep payments healthy even after 9 cross-skilled agents move to general from 16:00. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 85.2%.","trade_offs":["Cost: R2 is ₹825 more than R1 (₹13,782). R1 is also compliant but falls just short of target at 79.6%, with general at 77.1%.","Cheaper options don't recover service: no action gives 59.9% (general 47.6%), and P1 (₹750) actually drops to 57.9%.","P2 and P3 use an IVR outage message without a confirmed incident, which breaks policy CX-01. P3 also only reaches 76.6% despite costing ₹10,362.","Risk to payments: R2 pulls the most agents from payments (9 at 16:00-17:00) and cancels payments coaching. It relies on 10 payments agents accepting overtime to keep payments at 84.9%.","Customer impact: general callbacks run until 16:00, so some customers wait for a call back rather than being answered live."],"watch":"Watch how many agents take the overtime offer (28 + 8 on general, 10 on payments); a low uptake is the main risk to hitting target. Track new_offer_enquiry volume against the 5.2x trend and check general service level is recovering toward 78.6%. Check payments service level when the 9 agents move across at 16:00. No escalation is needed."}
